subject: actuarial-science
intro: Actuarial science leads into the risk professions — the actuaries who price uncertainty, the underwriters and claims professionals who apply those prices, and the risk specialists who guard balance sheets.

roles.title: Actuaries
roles.what: Analyse statistical data on mortality, accident, sickness, disability and retirement rates to construct probability tables, forecast risk and liability for future benefits, and set the insurance rates and reserves that keep promises payable.
roles.where: Life contingencies — mortality tables, insurance and annuity values, net premiums and reserves — plus Exam P probability and Exam FM interest theory are the credential syllabus you are already studying.

roles.title: Insurance Underwriters
roles.what: Review individual applications for insurance to evaluate the degree of risk involved and determine acceptance of applications — the commercial front line of the pricing tables actuaries build.
roles.where: Risk models — frequency and severity, compound distributions, fitting and selecting models — and credibility theory with bonus–malus systems teach the risk appraisal instincts accept-and-reject decisions rest on.

roles.title: Financial Risk Specialists
roles.what: Analyse and measure exposure to credit and market risk threatening the assets, earning capacity or economic state of an organisation, and make recommendations to limit that risk.
roles.where: Stochastic modelling of investments — portfolio mathematics, interest-rate models, asset–liability matching — and ruin theory with reinsurance are precisely this role's quantitative core.

roles.title: Claims Adjusters, Examiners, and Investigators
roles.what: Review settled claims to determine that payments and settlements are made in accordance with company practices and procedures, confer with legal counsel on claims requiring litigation, and may settle insurance claims.
roles.where: The professional practice unit — actuarial standards, reserving and capital regimes, communicating uncertainty — plus ruin and solvency concepts explain the reserves and rules every settled claim draws down.
